page.layout: Running head at top (ACTIS LIBER I.) with page number 5 at top right. One block of running text in a single column, continued from the previous page. Small section marks in the right margin. Two numbered entry headings, each followed by a paragraph. Catchword and gathering signature below the last line, at the right and centre foot.

main_text.p: sint[?] Christiani. Paulus etiam Corinthiis similia proponens, de templo non loquitur. Vnde in pri-mo Fastorum praedicti Mantuani:

Nam cum Cæsarei, gens sanguinolenta, tyranni Prædarentur oues Christi, nullasq; liceret Christigenis habitare urbes impune, ferarum Confortes facti, fines tenuere supremas Orbis, & ardentes Cancri feruentis arenas.
main_text.head: 2. ANACLETVS Atheniensis.
main_text.p: ANacletus Atheniensis, quem Irenæus post Linum ponit, doctrina & spiritu eximius, uerāq;[?] Ecclesiæ plantator assiduus, usq; ad Domitiani tyranni tempora uixit: cuius mandato, anno salutis nostræ 94. martyrio coronatus fuit. Epistolæ ac de-c.creta, quæ illi assignantur, de Episcoporum ordinatione ac primatu, horribilibus mendacijs scatet: quoniam, ut est apud Mantuanum, Per spelæa diu traxit syluatica uitam.
main_text.head: 3. CLEMENS Romanus.
main_text.p: Clemens Romanus, uir longè doctissimus, Ana-cleto succedens, religionem Christianam, non leges condendo, ut somniant Papicolæ: sed Euan-gelium prædicando, ac uirtutes operando, adauxit plurimum. Qualiter enim ille Rom. urbis regiones in Ecclesiis distribueret, qui uix domunculâ in ea-cdem habuerit, non intelligo.c[?] Aut quo modo puero-

page.notes: Top line: the first word is partly worn; read as "sint" with [?]. Verse stanza: printed lines joined into one paragraph. Abbreviation "uerāq;" (macron over a) and "domunculâ" are doubtful. "Ecclesiis" is worn and only partly legible. The section marks in the right margin are read as letters "c" (one doubtful). The catchword "rum" is the start of the next page. The paragraph ends at the page foot on the hyphenated word "puero-", so the text is not complete on this page.
